record.original_question: For each n >= 3, determine all complex structures on the smooth manifold underlying complex projective space CP^n, including the possible existence and classification of non-Kahler complex structures beyond the standard algebraic one.

evidence.quote: Problem 28. Consider the complex projective space Pn as a differentiable manifold with the usual differentiable structure. Determine all complex structures of Pn.
Both Problem 13 and Problem 28 are open for non-Kahlerian complex structures as soon as n >= 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$ and let $M$ denote the smooth manifold underlying the complex projective space $\mathbb{CP}^n$, equipped with its standard differentiable structure. A complex structure on $M$ is an integrable almost complex structure $J$ on $M$, equivalently the structure of a complex manifold whose underlying smooth manifold is $M$. Two such complex structures are equivalent if there is a biholomorphism between them inducing a diffeomorphism isotopic to the identity on $M$.

Determine all complex structures on $M$ up to equivalence. In particular, decide whether every complex structure on $M$ is biholomorphic to the standard algebraic structure of $\mathbb{CP}^n$, and if not, classify all non-Kähler complex structures on $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of complex structures on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ is a classical Hirzebruch problem. Under the Kähler assumption, uniqueness of the standard complex structure on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ is known (e.g., Hirzebruch–Kodaira and Yau for $n=2$, with extensions to higher $n$). However, without the Kähler hypothesis, the existence and classification of non-Kähler complex structures on the smooth manifold $\mathbb{CP}^n$ for $n \geq 3$ remains an open problem, as reflected in current surveys of non-Kähler complex geometry.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of the complex structure on Kähler manifolds of certain homotopy types
status_evidence.snippet: Uniqueness results are established under the Kähler hypothesis for manifolds of CP^n homotopy type.
status_evidence.claim: Kähler case is settled by Hirzebruch–Kodaira-type results.

status_evidence.title: EMS Surveys in Mathematical Sciences 12 (2025), 323–475
status_evidence.snippet: The geography of general compact complex manifolds and the boundary with the Kähler world remain largely mysterious.
status_evidence.claim: Non-Kähler classification problems on standard smooth manifolds, including projective spaces, remain open.
